chunks: Al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Musa ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Some of his companions asked him about using the siwak (tooth-stick) during the month of Ramadan. He said: 'It is permissible.' Some of them said: 'The moisture of the siwak enters the stomach.' He said: 'What do you say about the fresh (wet) siwak, whose moisture enters the throat?' He said: 'As for rinsing the mouth (madmadah), it is more moist than the fresh siwak. If a sayer says: 'Water is necessary for rinsing the mouth for the sake of the Sunnah,' then the siwak is necessary for the sake of the Sunnah which Jibril (peace be upon him) brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
ai.seo_question: Does using a tooth stick (siwak) break the fast in Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of siwak during Ramadan by employing a logical analogy (qiyas) with mouth rinsing (madmadah), noting that if the moisture from rinsing does not break the fast, neither does the moisture from siwak. He further elevates the practice by linking the Sunnah of siwak directly to the revelation of Jibril to the Prophet, thereby grounding the juristic ruling in prophetic tradition and highlighting the consistency of Shia fiqh in balancing ritual purity with practical ease.
